metaTitle: Door-to-door international moving from Panama | Global Moving
metaDescription: We move your household goods from Panama to all 5 continents. Inventory, export packing, ocean or air freight and customs at both ends, with a single coordinator.
entradilla: One person is accountable for the whole move, from the inventory in your living room to the last piece of furniture assembled in your new home.

secciones.h2: What door-to-door actually means here
parrafos: It means you never speak to the shipping line, the customs broker at destination, or the crew unloading on the other side. You speak to us. We hire and coordinate every link, and if something is delayed at a transshipment port you hear it from us before you notice it yourself.

The alternative some operators sell is port-to-port. It looks cheaper on the quote and turns out more expensive in practice, because clearance, inland transport and unloading at destination are yours to arrange, in a country whose paperwork you do not know and possibly in a language you do not speak.

secciones.h2: How the price is worked out
parrafos: By volume, not by weight. What drives the cost is how many cubic metres your goods take up once packed, and whether that fills a whole container or travels shared with other shipments. That is why the survey always comes first: a phone estimate is guesswork.

Three more things weigh on that volume: the destination and its transshipments, whether any pieces need a custom wooden crate, and whether the building at either end forces a long carry or an external hoist. All of it goes in the quote, not in a later invoice.

secciones.h2: Transit times, without the optimism
parrafos: An ocean shipment to Europe or North America moves in weeks, not days, and clearance at destination adds to that. Air freight cuts the time sharply and multiplies the cost, so it makes sense for what you need on arrival, not for the whole house.
One combination that works: the essentials by air, the rest by sea. We will suggest it if your arrival date and your shipment's do not line up.

incluye: Home survey and a fixed written quote
Valued inventory piece by piece, which also underpins the insurance
Export packing with new materials
Ocean or air freight and every transshipment
Export clearance in Panama and coordination of import clearance
Delivery inside the home, with furniture reassembly

faq.q: Can I take my appliances?
faq.a: Yes, but check the voltage at destination before paying freight on a fridge that will not switch on there. Panama runs on 110V and much of Europe on 220V. At the survey we tell you what is worth shipping and what is worth selling here.

faq.q: What cannot travel in a move?
faq.a: Nothing flammable or pressurised (paint, aerosols, gas cylinders), no perishable food, no plants with soil. Each country adds its own list. We give you the destination's list before packing, not on loading day.

faq.q: How early do I need to fix a date?
faq.a: As early as you can. Vessel space is booked ahead and peak seasons fill up. An approximate date is enough to hold the slot; the exact day is adjusted later.

resumen: We move your household goods from Panama to any destination in the world, door to door. We handle the inventory, export packing, ocean or air freight, customs clearance at both origin and destination, and delivery inside your new home. A single coordinator is accountable for the entire move, from start to finish.

h1: Moving within Panama, to an international standard
metaTitle: Local moving in Panama City and nationwide | Global Moving
metaDescription: Home moves within Panama City and to the interior, with the same packing and the same crew as an international move. Truck sized to your real volume.
entradilla: The same crew and the same materials we use to ship a house to Europe, applied to a move that takes one morning.

secciones.h2: Why local moves break more than they should
parrafos: Because they are treated as easy. Short trip, so people pack less, stack worse and assume that it will hold because it is only around the corner. Most damage in a local move happens in the lift and on the stairs, not on the road.

We pack to export standard even when the destination is fifteen minutes away. Moving blankets on every item, edge protectors on anything carried upright, double-wall cartons for fragile pieces. It costs a little more time on loading day and it avoids the awkward conversation at unloading.

secciones.h2: Apartment buildings and their rules
parrafos: Almost every building in the city requires the service lift to be booked, and many only allow moves on set days and hours. We handle that with both building administrations, the one you leave and the one you arrive at, before a single box moves.
If the lift will not take long items or the corridor will not turn, that gets solved at the survey, not on moving day with the truck waiting downstairs.

secciones.h2: Out to the interior
parrafos: To Coclé, Chiriquí, Veraguas, Los Santos or Bocas the work is the same but the trip is not: long roads, dirt for the last stretch, and sometimes a house the large truck cannot reach. We plan for that at the survey and size the vehicle accordingly, not the other way round.

incluye: Survey and a quote based on your home's real volume
Lift booking and permits with both building administrations
Packing with blankets, edge protectors and double-wall cartons
Dismantling and reassembly of beds, wardrobes and furniture
Truck sized to the load, not whichever one was free
Removal of all packing material when we finish

faq.q: How long does a move within the city take?
faq.a: A two-bedroom apartment is usually done in a morning if packing was done the day before. If you pack and move on the same day, allow a full day.

faq.q: Do you work weekends?
faq.a: Yes, and it is often the practical choice because many buildings only authorise moves on Saturday mornings. Book ahead.

faq.q: Can I pack myself and have you only load?
faq.a: You can, and it costs less. The honest caveat is that insurance treats owner-packed boxes differently: if a box you sealed arrives damaged, there is no way to establish how it was packed inside.

resumen: Moves within Panama City and to the interior of the country, with the same packing and the same care we apply to an international move. Ideal for changing homes, moving between apartments and relocating staff within Panama, with our own crew and a truck sized to the real volume of your home.

h1: Moving your office without stopping the business
metaTitle: Office relocation and corporate moving in Panama | Global Moving
metaDescription: Corporate moves planned after hours, labelled by workstation, with furniture, files and IT equipment reinstalled at the new site.
entradilla: The goal is not moving furniture. It is that on Monday every person finds their desk working.

secciones.h2: The real cost is the day you cannot invoice
parrafos: In an office move the expensive part is not the truck. It is the hours when thirty people cannot work. So we plan the move against the company's calendar rather than ours, which is why most of them run from Friday afternoon to Sunday.

In practice that means the move is prepared over days and executed in a short window. Labelling, partial dismantling and file packing happen with the office running; the physical move is concentrated into the weekend.

secciones.h2: Labelled by workstation, not by truck
parrafos: Every box, chair, monitor and drawer unit carries the code of its destination workstation, and we walk the new floor plan with the company's contact beforehand. That way unloading does not end in a room full of anonymous boxes nobody can place.
Staff only need to empty their personal drawer into the box labelled with their name. We do the rest.

secciones.h2: IT equipment and files
parrafos: Computers travel in antistatic packing and are reconnected at the right desk. What we do not do is touch configuration: we coordinate with the company's IT team, who are the ones who must confirm everything came back up.
Physical files move in numbered boxes with a signed handover, because much of it carries retention obligations and you need to be able to show it arrived complete.

incluye: Technical survey of both sites and a phased move plan
Work after hours and at weekends
Labelling by workstation against the destination floor plan
Dismantling and reassembly of modular furniture and workstations
Antistatic packing of IT equipment and reconnection
File relocation with a numbered handover record

faq.q: How far ahead should planning start?
faq.a: For an office of up to twenty desks, two or three weeks is enough. Above that, or with servers and files under retention rules, allow a month.

faq.q: Can we move in phases and keep operating?
faq.a: Yes, and that is the norm when stopping is not an option. Departments move over consecutive weekends, starting with whichever depends least on walk-in clients.

faq.q: What about things we no longer use?
faq.a: They get separated at the survey and decided before the move: storage, donation or disposal. Paying freight to move furniture nobody will use is inheriting a problem at the new site.

resumen: Corporate moves to international standard, planned so your company keeps operating. We work after hours and on weekends, label by workstation and reinstall furniture, files and IT equipment at the new site, so on Monday every person finds their desk up and running.

h1: Moving your pet out of Panama
metaTitle: International pet relocation from Panama | Global Moving
metaDescription: Veterinary certificate, export health permit, IATA-compliant crate and booking with airlines that accept live animals. Plus entry paperwork at destination.
entradilla: The hard part is not the flight. It is the chain of documents, which has expiry windows and does not forgive improvisation.

secciones.h2: The calendar rules everything
parrafos: Most countries require the veterinary certificate to be issued within a window of a few days before the flight, and some ask for laboratory tests months ahead. Break the order and the animal does not fly, and the whole process starts again.
So the first thing we build is the calendar, backwards from the flight date: what happens today, what at three months, what in the final week. That calendar is the work. The rest is executing it.

secciones.h2: The crate is not a detail
parrafos: Airlines refuse any crate at check-in that does not meet the IATA standard, and the criteria are concrete: the animal must be able to stand without lowering its head, turn around, and lie down. An undersized crate is the most common reason a booking is refused on the day.
We measure the animal and specify the exact size. Buy it weeks ahead so the animal sleeps in it before the trip: a pet entering its crate for the first time at the airport travels far worse.

secciones.h2: Breeds and routes with restrictions
parrafos: Flat-faced breeds (bulldogs, pugs, Persians and others) have breathing trouble in flight, and many airlines refuse them or accept them only in cabin. There are also temperature limits: above or below certain figures at any stop, the booking is cancelled.
That shapes the route and sometimes the date. Better to know while planning than at the counter.

incluye: Calendar built backwards from the flight date
Veterinary certificate arranged inside the valid window
Export health permit
Animal measured and an IATA-compliant crate in the right size
Booking with airlines that carry live animals on that route
Entry requirements and paperwork at destination

faq.q: How far ahead should I start?
faq.a: It depends on the destination. For the United States or Latin America weeks are usually enough. For the European Union, the United Kingdom or Australia allow months, because of laboratory tests and, in some cases, quarantine on arrival.

faq.q: Can my pet travel in the cabin with me?
faq.a: Only if the animal and its carrier stay under the airline's weight limit, which is usually low. Above that it travels in the pressurised, temperature-controlled hold of the same aircraft.

faq.q: What if I have a bird or an unusual pet?
faq.a: The process changes: beyond the health permit, CITES rules may apply if the species is protected. It can be done, but it has to be studied case by case and with more time.

resumen: Full logistics to move your pet along with the family. We arrange the veterinary health certificate, the export permit, the IATA-compliant travel crate and the booking with airlines that accept live animals, plus the entry paperwork in the destination country.

h1: Storage for your household goods in Panama City
metaTitle: Household goods storage in Panama City | Global Moving
metaDescription: Enclosed warehouses with 24/7 surveillance and access control, by the day or by the month. You pay for the volume you actually occupy, not a fixed unit.
entradilla: For the gap between leaving one home and entering the next, which is almost never zero days.

secciones.h2: When you need it
parrafos: Almost always for the same reason: the dates do not line up. You hand back the house on the 30th and receive the new one on the 15th; the visa is delayed; the purchase does not close in time; the container sails before you fly.
Storing your goods through that gap is cheaper than forcing a handover date on a property or paying a penalty on a missed sailing.

secciones.h2: You pay for what you occupy
parrafos: We do not rent you a fixed-size unit where you pay for the empty air. Your goods are stored packed and billed by the volume they actually take up, measured after packing.
That has one consequence worth knowing: if you are going to store, pack properly from the start. Badly stacked goods take up considerably more and cost more every month.

secciones.h2: What we will not take into storage
parrafos: Nothing flammable, no food, and nothing that attracts pests. Nor documents or valuable jewellery: bank safe deposit boxes exist for that, and that is where they belong.
We would rather say it now than discover it when the unit is opened six months later.

incluye: Enclosed warehouse with 24/7 surveillance and access control
Smoke detection
Intake inventory, with everything stored identified
Billing by real volume, by the day or by the month
Coordinated access if you need to retrieve something
Delivery to your home when the period ends

faq.q: Can I get something out while it is stored?
faq.a: Yes, with notice. This is not self storage with free access: we locate what you need and prepare it for collection.

faq.q: Is there a minimum period?
faq.a: No minimum number of months, but there is a minimum charge covering the handling in and out, which applies whether you store for a week or a year.

faq.q: Is it insured while in storage?
faq.a: Storage cover is arranged separately from transit cover and is calculated on the value declared in the inventory. We explain both before you sign.

resumen: Enclosed warehouses in Panama City with 24/7 surveillance, smoke detection and access control, to store your goods for days or for months. Useful while you close on a house, wait for a visa or settle a sailing date. You pay for the volume you actually occupy, not for a fixed unit.

h1: Consolidated ocean freight between Panama and Miami
metaTitle: Panama – Miami shared container consolidation | Global Moving
metaDescription: Your goods travel in a shared container with other shipments and you pay only for the cubic metres you use. The most affordable option when you do not fill a container.
entradilla: If your goods do not fill a container, paying for a whole one is buying empty space.

secciones.h2: Shared container versus exclusive container
parrafos: An exclusive container is paid for in full whether it travels loaded or half empty. In consolidation your goods share a container with other clients and you pay for the cubic metres you occupy. For a small apartment, or for part of a household, the price difference is large.

What you trade is time. The container sails once it is filled with other cargo, and at destination it has to be deconsolidated before delivery. If your date is fixed, an exclusive container is still the right answer and we will tell you so.

secciones.h2: Why this route in particular
parrafos: Panama and South Florida move steady traffic in both directions, and that is exactly what makes consolidation viable: there is enough cargo to fill containers regularly, so the wait stays reasonable.
It works both for people relocating and for anyone bringing accumulated purchases, furniture or equipment from the United States.

secciones.h2: How what you pay is measured
parrafos: Volume is measured once packed, not before, because packing takes space. An unprotected dining set measures less than the same set wrapped in blankets and edge protectors, and it is the second one that sails.
That is why the quote comes from the survey. A figure given over the phone from a list of furniture always falls short, and correcting it afterwards is the conversation nobody wants.

incluye: Survey and cubing of the goods once packed
Export packing
Space in a shared container on the Panama – Miami route
Shipping documentation
Deconsolidation at destination
Coordination of clearance and final delivery

faq.q: How much slower is it than an exclusive container?
faq.a: Slower, and by how much depends on when the container fills. We give you an estimated window at quoting and confirm once your cargo is loaded aboard.

faq.q: Does my shipment travel mixed with other people's?
faq.a: It shares a container, not space. Each shipment is identified and kept separate, and the intake inventory is what gets checked at deconsolidation.

faq.q: Can I ship a car this way?
faq.a: A vehicle has its own process and its own export documentation. It can be arranged, but it does not simply join a household consolidation: ask about it separately.

resumen: Consolidated freight service between Panama and Miami: your goods travel in a shared container with other shipments, so you only pay for the cubic metres you use. It is the most affordable option when you do not fill a full container and are not in a hurry over the arrival date.

h1: Customs clearance for your household goods
metaTitle: Customs clearance for household goods in Panama | Global Moving
metaDescription: We file your household goods with Panama's National Customs Authority and coordinate clearance at destination. Valued inventory, declaration and exemption paperwork where it applies.
entradilla: The paperwork is prepared before the container sails. Fixing it with the cargo already at port costs days of demurrage.

secciones.h2: The inventory is the key document
parrafos: Customs does not clear "a move": it clears a list of goods with declared values. That inventory is built during packing, piece by piece, and it is the same document that underpins the insurance and gets checked at destination.
A carelessly built inventory is the most common cause of a hold at port. And while cargo is held, storage charges run, paid by the owner of the goods.

secciones.h2: Used household goods are not merchandise
parrafos: Many countries treat the used household goods of a relocating resident under a different regime from commercial merchandise, sometimes with full or partial exemption. But that has to be proven with documents about the person, not just a list of furniture.

What qualifies varies by country, by visa or residence status, and by how long the goods have been owned. We tell you in advance what applies in your case, so there are no surprises once the cargo has arrived.

secciones.h2: At destination we work with local agents
parrafos: Import clearance is handled by an agent in the destination country, who knows its rules and is licensed to file there. We hire and coordinate them: you do not have to find one or negotiate with them.
That is the practical difference between buying door-to-door and buying freight only.

incluye: Valued inventory built during packing
Export declaration and documentation in Panama
Review of which regime applies to you and what proof is needed
Estimate of destination duties before the cargo sails
Appointment and coordination of the customs agent at destination
Follow-up until the cargo is released

faq.q: How much duty will I pay?
faq.a: It depends on the destination country, the regime that applies and the declared value. It is not a figure anyone can quote in general, but it can be estimated for your case before sailing, and that is what we do.

faq.q: Can I declare a low value to pay less?
faq.a: We will not recommend it. The declared value is also the ceiling on what insurance pays: undervalue it and, if the container is damaged, the settlement is calculated on that figure.

faq.q: What if customs wants a physical inspection?
faq.a: That is the authority's prerogative and it happens. If it does, we coordinate the opening and repacking. A well-built inventory makes the inspection quick.

resumen: We file your household goods with Panama's National Customs Authority and coordinate clearance at destination through our agent network. We prepare the valued inventory, the declaration and the exemption paperwork where it applies, and tell you the applicable duties in advance so there are no surprises at the port.

h1: Packing and unpacking with export-grade materials
metaTitle: Professional packing service for moving in Panama | Global Moving
metaDescription: Double-wall cartons, acid-free paper for china and artwork, blankets for furniture and ISPM 15 stamped wooden crates. At destination we unpack and take everything away.
entradilla: A container does not ride like a truck. It pitches for weeks. What survives a road trip does not survive that.

secciones.h2: Why the material matters more than it looks
parrafos: Supermarket cardboard has already made one trip, absorbed moisture and lost rigidity. Stacked six high inside a container crossing the Atlantic, it gives way. We use new double-wall cartons precisely because the weight is not carried by the contents, it is carried by the box underneath.
With china and artwork the problem is different: newsprint stains, and its ink reacts with glazes and varnish. That is why we use acid-free paper, which transfers nothing.

secciones.h2: Wooden crates and the ISPM 15 stamp
parrafos: Fragile, heavy and awkwardly shaped items travel in a custom wooden crate: marble, large mirrors, chandeliers, sculpture. The timber must carry the ISPM 15 stamp certifying phytosanitary treatment.
This is not red tape: a crate without that stamp can be refused at the destination port, and then it has to be repacked there, at your cost.

secciones.h2: We unpack at destination too
parrafos: Finishing a move surrounded by eighty empty boxes and a mountain of paper is the part nobody mentions. The service includes unpacking, reassembling furniture and taking all the material away.
You can book the outbound half only if you would rather open the boxes at your own pace. Decide that at quoting, not on arrival.

incluye: New double-wall cartons
Acid-free paper for china, glassware and artwork
Moving blankets and edge protectors for furniture
Custom wooden crates with the ISPM 15 stamp
Labelling by room and contents, tied to the inventory
Unpacking, reassembly and material removal at destination

faq.q: Can I pack part of it myself?
faq.a: Yes, and it lowers the cost. But anything you pack is recorded as owner-packed in the inventory, because insurance treats it differently: in a box sealed by the client there is no way to evidence how the contents were arranged.

faq.q: How long does packing a house take?
faq.a: A two-bedroom apartment, one day with the full crew. A large house with china, a library and paintings, two or three. It happens in the days before loading, not on the same day.

faq.q: What do I do with jewellery and documents?
faq.a: Those do not go in the move. Passports, deeds, jewellery and cash travel with you. We say it every time, and it is still what turns up inside a box most often.

resumen: We pack item by item with export-grade materials: double-wall cartons, acid-free paper for china and artwork, moving blankets for furniture and ISPM 15 stamped wooden crates for fragile pieces. At destination we unpack, reassemble the furniture and take away all the packing material.

h1: Insurance for your move, without the small print
metaTitle: International moving insurance from Panama | Global Moving
metaDescription: Domestic and international transit policies covering handling, the ocean or air leg and time in storage. We explain what each option covers and what value to declare.
entradilla: The question is not whether there is insurance. It is what exactly it covers, and on what figure it pays.

secciones.h2: Carrier liability is not insurance
parrafos: Every carrier is liable for what it carries, but that legal liability is capped and usually calculated by weight, not value. Translated: a two-kilo box with a camera inside is settled as two kilos of cargo, not as a camera.

Transit insurance is a separate thing and is bought separately. It pays on the value you declare in the inventory. Carrier liability does not replace it, and it is worth being clear on that beforehand rather than afterwards.

secciones.h2: What value to declare
parrafos: Replacement value, not purchase price. What it would cost to replace the item today, in the country where you will be living. A sofa bought eight years ago is not settled at what it cost then, nor at second-hand value, but at what an equivalent one costs there.
Under-declaring lowers the premium and raises the disappointment. Over-declaring achieves nothing, because settlement is paid against proven damage, not against the declared figure.

secciones.h2: The three legs that need covering
parrafos: Handling (loading, unloading, carrying), transit (ocean or air, with its transshipments) and time in storage if the goods are warehoused. These do not always sit in the same policy, and that is where the gaps appear.
If your move includes storage, ask explicitly whether those days are covered. We tell you without being asked, but it is worth knowing when comparing any operator.

incluye: Domestic or international transit policy to match the route
Cover for handling during loading and unloading
Cover for time in storage when warehousing is involved
Valued inventory as the basis of the cover
Written explanation of what each option covers and excludes
Support with the claim if one has to be filed

faq.q: How much does the insurance cost?
faq.a: It is a percentage of the declared inventory value, varying with the route and whether storage is involved. Because it is tied to declared value, the figure follows automatically once the inventory exists.

faq.q: What does a moving policy never cover?
faq.a: Pre-existing wear, hidden defects and, almost always, anything packed by the client. Cash, jewellery and documents are normally excluded too, which is why they should travel with you.

faq.q: If something arrives damaged, what do I do?
faq.a: Note it on the delivery record at that moment, before signing it off, and photograph it. A claim filed days later against a delivery signed without exception is far harder to sustain.

resumen: Domestic and international transit policies covering your goods during handling, the ocean or air leg and the time in storage. We explain what each option covers and what value to declare based on the inventory, so the coverage matches what you are actually shipping.
